title: Product description that sells
desc: Benefit-led copy with a hook and a clear call to action.

fields.ph: e.g. new moms, gift for teachers

tpl:
You are an expert Etsy copywriter. Write a product description for: {{product}}. Ideal buyer: {{buyer}}. Tone: {{tone}}.

Structure: a scroll-stopping first line, benefits (not just features), who it's for and why they'll love it, the key details/specs, and a clear call to action. Keep it scannable (short paragraphs, a little structure), weave in relevant keywords naturally (no stuffing), and sound human, not salesy. Give me 2 versions to choose from.

title: Etsy title (SEO-optimized)
desc: Front-loaded, long-tail, under 140 characters.
tpl:
You are an Etsy SEO specialist. Write 3 title options for: {{product}} (keywords: {{keywords}}; attributes: {{attrs}}).

Rules: each under 140 characters, front-load the highest-intent long-tail phrase buyers actually search, use natural multi-word phrases separated by " | ", cover different search angles (style, use, gift/occasion), and avoid keyword stuffing or repetition. Tell me which is strongest and why, and which to A/B test.

title: 13 Etsy tags
desc: All 13 slots used well — long-tail, buyer-intent.
tpl:
You are an Etsy SEO expert. Generate exactly 13 tags for: {{product}} (title: {{title}}).

Each tag ≤ 20 characters, multi-word where possible (no wasted single words), a mix of broad and specific long-tail buyer-intent phrases, include occasion/gift/style angles, and don't repeat the same root word across tags. Align them with the title. Mark 2 you'd A/B test and say why.

title: Refresh a stale listing
desc: Diagnose why it's not selling and fix the biggest lever.

fields.ph: e.g. views but no sales / no views

tpl:
You are an Etsy growth consultant. My listing isn't performing (problem: {{issue}}). Title: {{title}}. Product: {{product}}.

Diagnose the most likely causes (SEO, first photo, price, or copy) based on the problem, then give me a rewritten title, tag changes, a stronger first description line, and one photo/CTA fix. Prioritize the SINGLE highest-impact change I should make first, and why.

title: Keyword brainstorm
desc: 20 long-tail phrases grouped by buyer intent.
tpl: You are an Etsy keyword strategist. Brainstorm 20 long-tail keyword phrases a buyer would type to find: {{product}}. Group them by intent (broad, specific/descriptive, occasion/gift, style/aesthetic). Flag the 5 with likely best demand-to-competition balance, and remind me to validate them in Etsy search / eRank before committing (don't invent search volumes).

title: Category, attributes & occasions
desc: Fill every field Etsy uses to surface you.
tpl: You are an Etsy listing expert. For {{product}}, recommend the best Etsy category, every relevant attribute I should fill (color, material, style, occasion, recipient, holiday), and 3 gift/occasion angles to add. Explain how filling these gives me more search surfaces and filter appearances.

title: Listing variations & options
desc: Add options that lift conversion and order value.
tpl: You are an Etsy merchandising expert. Suggest smart variations for {{product}} (size, color, format, personalization, bundle), how to present them so buyers self-select, which option to feature as the default, and the pricing implications. Keep it simple enough to manage.

title: Product photo shot list
desc: What each of the 10 photo slots should show.
tpl: You are an Etsy conversion photographer. Give a shot list for the 10 photo slots for {{product}}: hero, scale/context, detail/quality, in-use/styled, variations, packaging/unboxing, and an info graphic. For each, say what it communicates and why it helps conversion. Add one tip for a strong, thumbnail-friendly first photo.

title: Instagram caption
desc: Hook, story, CTA and a smart hashtag set.
tpl: You are a social media manager for handmade brands. Write 3 Instagram captions for: {{product}} (goal: {{goal}}, tone: {{tone}}). Each: a scroll-stopping first line, a short benefit or story, and a clear CTA. Add one set of 15 relevant hashtags (mixed reach + niche). On-brand, not spammy.

title: Reels / TikTok hook + script
desc: Stop the scroll in 3 seconds, then a shot list.
tpl: You are a short-form video expert. For {{product}}, give 3 hook lines for the first 3 seconds, then a 15–30s script for this idea: {{idea}} — as a shot list with on-screen text and a CTA. Optimize for watch-through and shares. Add a trending-audio suggestion approach (how to pick one).

title: Pinterest pin description
desc: Pinterest SEO that keeps driving traffic.
tpl: You are a Pinterest marketing expert. For {{product}} (keywords: {{keywords}}), write a keyword-rich pin title and description optimized for Pinterest search, 3 different pin angle ideas, and 3 board suggestions. Describe the ideal pin image (vertical, text overlay). Keep it evergreen so it keeps driving traffic.

title: 2-week content calendar
desc: 14 batchable posts across platforms.
tpl: You are a content strategist. Plan a 14-day content calendar for my shop ({{shop}}) featuring {{products}}. Mix product, behind-the-scenes, value/tips, social proof/UGC, and promo posts. For each day: a one-line idea, the platform, and the format. Keep it low-effort and batchable, and note which posts to repurpose across platforms.

title: Product launch announcement
desc: Build anticipation and convert on day one.
tpl: You are a launch strategist. Write launch content for {{product}} (offer: {{offer}}): a teaser post, the launch-day post, an email blurb, and an Etsy shop announcement. Build anticipation, state the offer, add honest urgency, and a clear CTA. Give 2 tone options for the main post.

title: Hashtag sets
desc: Rotatable sets sized for reach vs competition.
tpl: You are a social media strategist. Create 3 hashtag sets for {{product}} in the {{niche}} niche — broad, niche, and community — about 15 each, balanced for reach vs competition (avoid banned/overused ones). Explain how to rotate them to avoid looking spammy.

title: Welcome email
desc: Turn a new subscriber into a first-time buyer.
tpl: You are an email marketer for small shops. Write a warm welcome email for {{shop}} (incentive: {{incentive}}): a friendly intro, what to expect, the incentive, 2–3 best-sellers, and a clear CTA. Keep it short and on-brand. Include a subject line and preview text, plus one A/B subject alternative.

title: Welcome email sequence (3 emails)
desc: A nurture flow that builds trust and sells.
tpl: You are an email strategist. Outline a 3-email welcome sequence for {{shop}} (incentive: {{incentive}}): Email 1 (welcome + incentive), Email 2 (brand story / value), Email 3 (best-sellers + social proof + urgency). For each: the goal, subject line + preview, key points, and CTA. Note the send timing between them.

title: Abandoned cart email
desc: Recover lost sales without being pushy.
tpl: You are a conversion copywriter. Write an abandoned-cart email (and a short 2nd follow-up) for {{shop}}: a friendly reminder, reassurance (reviews, easy returns, secure), gentle urgency, and an optional small incentive for the 2nd email. Include subject lines + preview text. Keep it human.

title: Sale / promo email
desc: Clear offer, urgency, hero products.
tpl: You are an email marketer. Write a promo email for {{shop}}: offer {{offer}}, running {{dates}}. Lead with the offer, add urgency/deadline, feature 2–3 hero products, and a strong CTA. Scannable. Subject line + preview + one A/B subject.

title: Review request message
desc: Politely earn more reviews (policy-safe).
tpl: You are a customer-experience expert. Write a polite post-purchase message asking for a review of {{product}}: thank them, make leaving a review easy, and keep it low-pressure. IMPORTANT: do not offer incentives for reviews (against Etsy policy) — just make it genuine. Keep it short and warm.

title: Respond to a negative review
desc: Calm, professional, reputation-protecting reply.
tpl: You are a customer-service expert protecting a shop's reputation. Given this review — {{review}} (context: {{context}}) — write a calm, professional PUBLIC reply that acknowledges their experience, stays non-defensive, and shows future readers you're reasonable and solution-focused. Then write a private message to make it right. Don't argue or over-apologize.

title: Reply to a positive review
desc: Turn a happy buyer into a repeat customer.
tpl: You are a loyalty-focused shop owner. Write a warm, genuine reply to this positive review — {{review}} — that thanks them specifically, reinforces what they loved, and subtly invites them back or to share the shop, without sounding scripted. Keep it short.

title: Answer a customer question
desc: Clear, complete, anticipates the follow-up.
tpl: You are a friendly, knowledgeable shop owner. Answer this customer question clearly and completely: {{question}} (relevant info: {{context}}). Anticipate the likely follow-up and address it, stay on-brand and warm, and end helpfully. Keep it concise.

title: Handle a refund / return
desc: Fair, empathetic, de-escalating response.
tpl: You are an experienced shop owner. Write a fair, empathetic response to this refund/return request: {{situation}} (policy: {{policy}}). Acknowledge their frustration, offer clear solutions (refund / replacement / store credit) consistent with the policy, and de-escalate. Protect both the relationship and the shop. Give a firm-but-kind version too.

title: Shipping delay message
desc: Proactive, confident, goodwill-building.
tpl: You are a customer-experience pro. Write a proactive message about a shipping delay: {{situation}}. Be honest and apologetic but confident, give a clear new timeline, and offer a goodwill gesture if warranted. Reassure them and reduce the chance of a negative review.

title: Custom order inquiry reply
desc: Set scope, expectations and next steps.
tpl: You are a shop owner handling custom orders. Reply to this request: {{request}}. Clarify the scope, set expectations (timeline, price range, revisions, what you need from them), and lay out next steps to confirm and quote. Warm and professional, and protect your time and margins.

title: Thank-you note / insert
desc: Delight buyers and earn follows and reviews.

fields.ph: e.g. follow on IG, tag us

tpl: You are a brand-experience designer. Write a short thank-you note for a package insert from {{shop}}: genuine gratitude, a small moment of delight, care/use tip if relevant, and a soft ask ({{ask}}). Keep it on-brand and human — 3–4 lines. Give 2 versions.

title: Shop 'About' story
desc: Build trust with an authentic origin story.

fields.ph: who you are, why you started, what's special

tpl: You are a brand storyteller. Write a compelling Etsy About section from this: {{shop}}. Include your story, mission, what makes you different, and why buyers can trust you. Authentic and warm (not corporate), scannable, and end with an inviting line. Give a shorter and a longer version.

title: Brand voice & tagline
desc: Define your vibe and nail a tagline.

fields.ph: what you sell + the feeling you want

tpl: You are a brand strategist. From this — {{shop}} — define a brand voice (3 adjectives + a short do/don't list) and give 5 tagline options with the vibe each conveys. Recommend the strongest and where to use it (shop title, about, banner).

title: Shop policies (clear & friendly)
desc: Reduce disputes with plain-language policies.

fields.ph: shipping, returns, processing time, custom orders

tpl: You are an e-commerce operations expert. Turn these details — {{details}} — into clear, friendly, professional shop policies (shipping, returns/exchanges, processing time, custom orders). Plain language that sets expectations and reduces disputes, while staying fair and on-brand.

title: Shop announcement banner
desc: The top-of-shop line that informs and converts.

fields.ph: e.g. sale, current processing time, restock

tpl: You are a conversion copywriter. Write 3 short shop-announcement options featuring: {{news}}. Each should inform buyers, build trust (processing time, shipping), and include a light CTA. Keep them brief and scannable.

title: Find & phrase your USP
desc: Say clearly why buyers should pick you.

fields.ph: what you sell + how you're different

tpl: You are a positioning strategist. From my shop — {{shop}} (competitors: {{competitors}}) — identify what genuinely makes me different, phrase 3 clear USP statements, and tell me where to use each (title, about, product copy). Avoid generic claims like "high quality".

title: Product FAQ section
desc: Answer hesitations to boost conversion.
tpl: You are a conversion copywriter. Write a helpful FAQ (6–8 Q&As) for {{product}} that answers the real hesitations buyers have (sizing, materials, shipping, personalization, care, digital use). Answers should reassure and reduce pre-sale questions. Keep them concise and friendly.

title: New product ideas from a trend
desc: On-brand ideas that fit a rising trend.
tpl: You are an Etsy product strategist. Suggest 8 product ideas that fit my shop ({{shop}}) and this trend ({{trend}}). For each: a one-line why-it-could-sell and a rough difficulty. Flag the top 2 to test first, and remind me to validate real demand (Etsy search / eRank) before building.

title: Bundle & upsell ideas
desc: Raise average order value with smart sets.
tpl: You are a merchandising strategist. From my products — {{products}} — propose bundles/sets and upsell/cross-sell pairings, with a catchy name and a pricing angle for each that raises average order value while feeling like a deal to the buyer.

title: Pricing strategy helper
desc: Price for profit and positioning (you confirm numbers).
tpl: You are a pricing consultant. Help me price {{product}} (costs: {{costs}}; competitor range: {{competitors}}). Walk through: covering costs + Etsy fees + a real profit margin, positioning vs competitors, psychological pricing (charm pricing, anchoring), and bundle/discount strategy. Give a recommended price RANGE with reasoning — I'll confirm my actual numbers.

title: Seasonal product angle
desc: Reposition an existing product for the season.
tpl: You are a seasonal-selling expert. Reposition {{product}} for {{season}}: new keywords, a gift angle, listing tweaks (title/tags/first photo), and a mini promo idea. Tell me the lead time — how early to list to catch the search wave.

title: Product name brainstorm
desc: Memorable, searchable names in your vibe.
tpl: You are a naming expert. Brainstorm 15 product names for {{product}} in a {{vibe}} vibe — memorable and still searchable — grouped by style. For each group, note the trade-off between brand-y and SEO-friendly, and recommend a naming approach for Etsy.

title: Overcome buyer objections
desc: Address the reasons people hesitate to buy.
tpl: You are a conversion strategist. List the top 5 reasons buyers hesitate on {{product}}, and for each, the exact copy or reassurance to address it — and where it should live (title, first photo, description, FAQ, reviews). Make it specific to this product.

title: Etsy Ads keyword picks
desc: What to promote and which terms to target.
tpl: You are an Etsy Ads specialist. For {{product}} (title: {{title}}), suggest which high-intent keywords/phrases to target, which broad ones to consider excluding, and a sensible starter daily-budget logic. Remind me to check the Ads search-terms report weekly and cut/scale based on real data (don't promise specific results).

title: Ad / promo copy
desc: Short, benefit-led ad variations.
tpl: You are a direct-response copywriter. Write 3 short ad variations for {{product}} (offer/angle: {{offer}}): a headline + one line each, benefit-led with a clear CTA. Give one curiosity-driven, one benefit-driven, and one offer-driven version.

title: What should I promote?
desc: Turn your stats into ad decisions.
tpl: You are an Etsy growth analyst. From my data — {{shop}} — tell me which listings to promote and which to fix first: high views + low sales usually means the listing/photo/price needs work (don't just throw ads at it); high-converting listings are the ones to scale with ads. Give me a prioritized action list and the logic.

title: 30-day growth plan
desc: A focused month of high-leverage actions.
tpl: You are an Etsy growth coach. Build a realistic 30-day plan for {{shop}} toward this goal: {{goal}}. Break it into weekly focuses (SEO fixes, new listings, content, email, an ads test), with the 20% of actions that drive 80% of results first. Keep it doable for a solo seller.

title: Influencer / collab outreach
desc: Value-first outreach that gets replies.

fields.ph: e.g. a small IG creator in your niche

tpl: You are an influencer-marketing expert. Write a short, personalized outreach message from {{shop}} to {{target}} proposing a collaboration. Lead with genuine value for them, keep it low-pressure, and make one clear, easy ask. Give a DM version and an email version.

title: Validate a product idea
desc: Go / test / skip before you build it.
tpl: You are a lean e-commerce advisor. Give me a validation framework for this idea: {{idea}}. Cover demand signals to check, competition to scan, how to differentiate, a quick profit sanity check, and a clear go / test / skip decision logic. List exactly what I should look up on Etsy/eRank — do not invent numbers.

title: Competitor analysis checklist
desc: Learn from top shops and find gaps.
tpl: You are a market analyst. Give me a checklist to analyze the top competitors in the {{niche}} niche: their titles, tags, photos, pricing, reviews, and what buyers praise vs complain about. Then show me how to turn those findings into 3 concrete opportunities for my shop.

title: Find an underserved sub-niche
desc: Narrow down to where you can win.
tpl: You are a niche strategist. Within {{broad}}, brainstorm 8 narrower sub-niches or specific buyer segments that may be underserved. For each: who it's for, why it might be underserved, and a product angle. Flag the 2 most promising and what to check to confirm.

title: Seasonal selling calendar
desc: Know what to list and when.
tpl: You are an Etsy seasonal strategist. Map the next 3–4 months of selling opportunities for {{shop}}: relevant holidays, seasons and events, when to LIST for each (lead time before the search peak), and a product/keyword angle per opportunity. Prioritize the 3 biggest for my shop.

title: Listing SEO self-audit
desc: A checklist to fix a listing yourself.
tpl: You are an Etsy SEO auditor. Give me a step-by-step self-audit checklist for a listing{{product}}: title (front-loading, long-tail, length), all 13 tags, attributes, first-photo quality, description keywords, and quality signals (reviews, completeness). For each item, how to tell if it's weak and exactly how to fix it.

title: Make sense of my Etsy stats
desc: Read your numbers and know the next move.

fields.ph: views, visits, conversion rate, favorites, etc.

tpl: You are an Etsy analyst. Interpret my stats: {{stats}}. Tell me what looks healthy vs a red flag (e.g. views but low conversion = listing/price issue; low views = SEO/reach issue), the likely causes, and the top 3 actions to take next. Ask me for any key number that's missing.

title: Press / feature pitch
desc: Get featured on a blog, gift guide or roundup.
tpl: You are a PR specialist for small brands. Write a concise pitch email to a blogger/editor to feature {{shop}}. Lead with the angle ({{angle}}) and why it's relevant now, keep it skimmable, make it easy to say yes (offer images/samples), and end with a low-friction next step. Include a subject line.

title: Wholesale inquiry reply
desc: Handle a wholesale request professionally.
tpl: You are a wholesale/operations expert. Reply to this wholesale inquiry: {{inquiry}}. Professionally clarify quantities, terms, minimum order, your pricing approach (protect margins), lead time, and next steps. Warm but businesslike. If it's not a fit, give a polite decline version too.

title: Back-in-stock announcement
desc: Reward waiting customers and create urgency.
tpl: You are a marketing copywriter. Write back-in-stock announcements for {{product}} — one email and one social post — that reward customers who waited, create honest urgency (limited quantity if true), and drive a fast CTA. Include a subject line for the email.

title: Weekly seller task plan
desc: Focus your limited hours on what moves the needle.
tpl: You are a productivity coach for solo sellers. Build a weekly plan given ~{{hours}} hours and these priorities: {{priorities}}. Batch similar tasks (listing, photography, marketing, orders, admin), put the highest-leverage work first, and protect time for the ONE thing that grows sales. Present it as a simple day-by-day plan.

title: Batch a month of content
desc: Create weeks of posts in one sitting.
tpl: You are a content-batching coach. Give me a plan to create a month of content for {{shop}} (featuring {{products}}) in one focused session: content themes, a shot/prompt list to capture at once, captions to draft in bulk, and a simple way to schedule it. Keep it realistic for a busy solo seller.
